Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.

The **dual connection** on the smooth bundle $E^*$ of [[def-connection-on-a-smooth-vector-bundle]] is characterized by
$$ (\nabla^*_X\alpha)(s)=X(\alpha(s))-\alpha(\nabla_Xs).$$
The right side is function-linear in $s$: replacing $s$ by $fs$ introduces $X(f)\alpha(s)$ once with each sign, so those terms cancel.

Here is the construction, including well-definedness. In a frame $e$ write $s=eu$ and write $\alpha$ with dual coefficient column $a$, so $\alpha(s)=a^Tu$. The coordinate formula [[prop-local-coordinate-formula-for-a-bundle-connection]] gives
$$X(a^Tu)-a^T(X(u)+\omega(X)u)=(X(a)-\omega(X)^Ta)^Tu.$$
Thus the required coefficients are $X(a)-\omega(X)^Ta$, and the local connection matrix in the dual frame is $-\omega^T$. These local rules are smooth, real-linear and obey the section Leibniz rule by the scalar product rule. On an overlap both give the intrinsic displayed pairing formula; agreement against every local frame section forces equality of the dual covectors. They therefore glue to a connection, equivalently by [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]]. Testing against a basis also proves uniqueness. This verifies the implicit characterization rather than assuming that it defines an operator.

The derivative on scalar functions is $X(f)$; duality preserves the evaluation pairing with that scalar connection. For rank one the matrix changes sign; for rank zero evaluation and all coefficients are empty. Zero sections give zero derivatives, while empty bases give the unique operator. This construction is local and canonical from the given connection and requires no choice axiom.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

abla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature operator, Ricci contraction, and sign convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. For a real $C^3$ one-form $A$, define $(\Box A)_b:=g^{ac}
abla_a
abla_c A_b$, $(\operatorname{div}A):=
abla^aA_a$, and $(PA)_b:=\Box A_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^cA_c$. Then

$$ 
abla^a(dA)_{ab}=(PA)_b-
abla_b(\operatorname{div}A). $$

The same identity holds for a complex one-form after complex-linear extension. The identity is local and uses no field equation, gauge condition, boundary condition, or physical assumption.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].

The complex exponential is entire, and

$$ \exp'(z)=\exp z $$

for every $z\in\mathbb C$.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open, let $a\in U$, and write $f=u+iv:U\to\mathbb C$. The following are equivalent:

1. $f$ is complex differentiable at $a$.
2. Under $\mathbb C\cong\mathbb R^2$, the map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and $Df(a)$ is multiplication by a complex number.
3. The map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and $\partial_{\bar z}f(a)=0$.
4. The map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations

$$ u_x(a)=v_y(a),\qquad u_y(a)=-v_x(a). $$

When these conditions hold,

$$ f'(a)=u_x(a)+iv_x(a)=v_y(a)-iu_y(a)=\partial_zf(a). $$

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Complex conjugation is a real-field automorphism satisfying
$$\overline{z+w}=\overline z+\overline w,\qquad \overline{zw}=\overline z\,\overline w,\qquad \overline{\overline z}=z.$$

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. $$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]), let $F$ be its integral function
([[def-the-integral-function]]), and let $c \in [a,b]$ be a point at which $f$ is
continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $F$ is differentiable at $c$ as a
function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(c) \;=\; f(c) .$$

At $c = a$ and $c = b$ this is the one-sided statement, which is what
[[def-derivative]] means at those points: every point of a nondegenerate interval
is a limit point of it, so $F'(c)$ is a meaningful symbol at every $c \in [a,b]$,
and the difference quotient is taken over $[a,b] \setminus \{c\}$.

primitive of $f$ there**: $F' = f$ at every point of $[a,b]$.

differ from $f(c)$; both are exhibited on the companion page, by
an integrable function with no primitive and by a false
statement about the integral function.

In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Nonemptiness of $X$ is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for $X = \emptyset$ the
image is empty and has neither a supremum nor a maximum. No choice principle is
used.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Use the energy-condition definitions of [[def-emg-pointwise-energy-conditions]] and the matter and Maxwell tensor definitions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. At every point of an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian domain, the Maxwell tensor $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ of that definition is symmetric, trace-free, and satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. Its observer energy density and energy flux in a positively oriented orthonormal rest frame are

$$u=\frac{|E|^2/c^2+|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad \frac{E\times B}{\mu_0c},$$

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff \epsilon\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$\mathrm{SEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+3p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\epsilon\ge|p|.$$

At a point, finite sums of tensors satisfying any one of these conditions still satisfy that condition; in particular $T_{\mathrm{EM}}+T_m$ satisfies all four for nonnegative dust. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

derivations.claim: Exterior differentiation is real-linear and the Hodge star is real-linear by [F5], so $dF_\delta=\delta\,dF_0=0$ and $d(\star_gF_\delta)=\delta\,d(\star_gF_0)=0$. Each term in the Maxwell tensor of [F1] is quadratic in $F$, hence $T_{\mathrm{EM}}(g,F_\delta)=\delta^2T_{\mathrm{EM}}(g,F_0)$.

The definitions in [F1] give $T_m(\eta\rho,U)=\eta T_m(\rho,U)$ and $j(\eta\sigma,U)=\eta j(\sigma,U)$. On $\{\rho>0\}$, $(\eta\sigma)/(\eta\rho)=\sigma/\rho$. The force equation in [F3] therefore has both sides multiplied by $\eta$ if $F$ and $U$ are held fixed.

At any point where $F_0\ne0$, choose a future unit observer and its positively oriented orthonormal rest frame. Then $E$ and $B$ cannot both vanish, since the field components are $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ by [F1]. With $\mu_0>0$, the density formula [F2] gives $u>0$. Minkowski space has $G_{ab}=0$; with $\Lambda=0$ and $T_m=0$, the Einstein equation would require $0=\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}$, contradicted by this positive observer contraction and $\kappa>0$ from [F1].

The Coulomb energy density on $\mathcal A_\ell$ is $\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|\mathbf E|^2=\frac{Q^2}{32\pi^2\varepsilon_0 r^4}$ by [F2] and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ from [F1], where $r=|\mathbf x|$. Apply [F6] to this nonnegative radial Borel function, restricted to $\ell<r<2\ell$, to obtain $ \mathcal E_\ell=4\pi\int_\ell^{2\ell}\frac{Q^2}{32\pi^2\varepsilon_0r^4}r^2\,dr =\frac{Q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_\ell^{2\ell}r^{-2}\,dr. $ The polar-coordinate measure and the field profile are only used on the finite annulus.

The hypotheses of [F4] are exactly the fixed vacuum metric and smooth source-free $F_0$ in [A1]. Applying [F4] with the specified real scalar $\delta$ gives $\mathscr R(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2T_{\mathrm{EM}}(g,F_0)$; step 1.1 also verifies directly that the scaled field remains source-free and that its stress has this quadratic scaling.

The sourced Maxwell equation is $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ by [F1]; replacing $j$ by $\eta j$ while leaving $F$ fixed changes its right-hand side to $-\eta\mu_0j^b$, so it remains the same equation only when $(\eta-1)j=0$. If instead $(F,j)\mapsto(\eta F,\eta j)$, the Maxwell equation is preserved by linearity, but step 1.1 scales $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ quadratically while step 1.2 scales $T_m$ linearly; the dust force equation then also has its left side scale by $\eta$ and its right side by $\eta^2$. These unequal degrees show why this scaling is not a general coupled-solution construction, while leaving special cancellations open.

The primitive $-r^{-1}$ has derivative $r^{-2}$ on $(0,\infty)$ by [F7], so $\int_\ell^{2\ell}r^{-2}\,dr=\ell^{-1}-(2\ell)^{-1}=(2\ell)^{-1}$. Hence $\mathcal E_\ell=Q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0\ell)$. For every $M>0$, choosing $0<\ell<Q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0M)$ gives $\mathcal E_\ell>M$; therefore the shell energies diverge as $\ell\downarrow0$ at fixed $Q\ne0$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for its canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, so the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$ exists by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $O\subseteq M$ be open and let $F$ be a $C^1$ alternating covariant two-tensor field on $O$ (a two-form); define $F^\sharp$ by $g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$. Fix $m,c>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, an event $x_0\in O$, and $U_0\in T_{x_0}M$ with $g(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ future directed. Then the initial-value problem

$$\dot x=U,\qquad \nabla_UU=(q/m)F^\sharp(U),\qquad (x(\tau_0),U(\tau_0))=(x_0,U_0)$$

has a unique local $C^2$ solution on an open proper-time interval containing $\tau_0$. Any two solutions with these initial data agree on every connected part of their common domain containing $\tau_0$. Along the solution, $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ remains future directed. The result is local; it asserts no completeness or global existence for arbitrary external fields.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with strictly positive derivative
(including one-sided endpoint derivatives), comparing the increment over the
actual image interval, are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]), let $F$ be its integral function
([[def-the-integral-function]]), and let $c \in [a,b]$ be a point at which $f$ is
continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $F$ is differentiable at $c$ as a
function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(c) \;=\; f(c) .$$

At $c = a$ and $c = b$ this is the one-sided statement, which is what
[[def-derivative]] means at those points: every point of a nondegenerate interval
is a limit point of it, so $F'(c)$ is a meaningful symbol at every $c \in [a,b]$,
and the difference quotient is taken over $[a,b] \setminus \{c\}$.

**Consequently, if $f$ is continuous on the whole of $[a,b]$, then $F$ is a
primitive of $f$ there**: $F' = f$ at every point of $[a,b]$.

**Continuity at $c$ is a hypothesis and it cannot be dropped.** For an integrable
$f$ that is discontinuous at $c$, $F'(c)$ may fail to exist, and it may exist and
differ from $f(c)$; both are exhibited on the companion page, by
an integrable function with no primitive and by a false
statement about the integral function.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Let $F$ be an ordered field ([[def-ordered-field]]) and let $x, y \in F$, with
$|x|$ the absolute value ([[def-abs-value]]). Then

$$|x| \ge 0; \quad |x| = 0 \iff x = 0; \quad -|x| \le x \le |x|; \quad |-x| = |x|; \quad |xy| = |x|\,|y|;$$

and, for every $c > 0$, one has $|x| < c \iff -c < x < c$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric, connection, curvature sign, length-coordinate SI convention and constants of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Let $\theta\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ be dimensionless, set $k:=d\theta$, and assume that $k$ is nowhere zero and $g^{-1}(k,k)=0$. Let $a_0,a_1\in C^3(U;T^*M\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$; this means that the real and imaginary parts of their coefficients are $C^3$ in every smooth chart. Complex tensor operations and $\nabla$ are extended componentwise and complex-linearly. Define

$$ (\Box a)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c a_b,\qquad (Pa)_b:=(\Box a)_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^c a_c,\qquad d_1:=\nabla^a(a_1)_a, $$

and define the first-order operator

$$ (La)_b:=2k^c\nabla_c a_b+(\nabla_c k^c)a_b. $$

Assume pointwise on $U$ that

$$ g^{-1}(k,a_0)=0,\qquad La_0=0,\qquad iLa_1+Pa_0=0,\qquad ik^a(a_1)_a+\nabla^a(a_0)_a=0. $$

These are finite-order ansatz constraints; they assert neither initial data nor a global solution of the transport equations. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, set

$$ A_\epsilon:=\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}(a_0+\epsilon a_1),\qquad F_\epsilon:=dA_\epsilon. $$

Then $dF_\epsilon=0$ and the exact Maxwell divergence residual is

$$ \nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab} =e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[-i\epsilon k_b d_1+ \epsilon^2\bigl((Pa_1)_b-\nabla_b d_1\bigr)\right]. $$

The field-strength expansion is also exact:

$$ F_\epsilon=e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[ik\wedge a_0+ \epsilon(da_0+ik\wedge a_1)+\epsilon^2da_1\right]. $$

For units, take $[k]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[a_0]=[a_1]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[d_1]=\mathrm T$, $[Pa_1]=[\nabla d_1]=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, and $[\epsilon]=[\theta]=1$. In one chart and for a compact coordinate set $K$, define

$$ \|S\|_{\infty,K}:= \begin{cases} \max_I\max_{x\in K}|S_I(x)|,&K\ne\varnothing,\\ 0,&K=\varnothing, \end{cases} $$

where $I$ ranges over the finitely many components of the real or complex tensor in that chart. If $K\ne\varnothing$ and finite constants $K_0,D_0,C_0,B_0,B_1\ge0$ satisfy

$$ \|k\|_{\infty,K}\le K_0,\quad \|d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le D_0,\quad \|Pa_1-\nabla d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le C_0,\quad \|da_0+ik\wedge a_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_0,\quad \|da_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_1, $$

then

$$ \|\nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab}\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon K_0D_0+\epsilon^2C_0,\qquad \|F_\epsilon-e^{i\theta/\epsilon}ik\wedge a_0\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon B_0+\epsilon^2B_1. $$

Taking real parts gives real potentials and fields with the same bounds. Every local integral curve of $k^\sharp$ is an affinely parametrized null geodesic and lies in a level set of $\theta$. Along each such ray, a nonzero scalar transport amplitude

$$ \mathcal A(\lambda)=\mathcal A(\lambda_0) \exp\left(-\frac12\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}(\nabla_c k^c)(\gamma(s))\,ds\right) $$

is defined on every compact subinterval of the ray. The one-form $e:=a_0/\mathcal A$ is transverse and parallel transported. At each point the leading polarization is the class $[a_0]\in k^\perp/\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{k\}$, where $k^\perp=\{a:g^{-1}(k,a)=0\}$. This quotient is a two-dimensional complex vector space with a positive induced Hermitian form, and $a_0\mapsto a_0+\beta k$ leaves $k\wedge a_0$ unchanged. If $a_0$ is proportional to $k$, the leading field vanishes. No convergence of a WKB series, existence of amplitudes satisfying the constraints, exact-solution error estimate, or behavior through caustics is asserted.

Use the field, stress, matter, unit and curvature conventions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and define the Einstein residual for the source-free field model by

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F). $$

Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $F_0$ be a smooth real two-form with $dF_0=0$ and $d(\star_gF_0)=0$. For every real dimensionless $\delta$, the field $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ obeys the same source-free Maxwell equations and

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2 T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0). $$

This is an exact residual identity on the fixed metric. If $\delta\ne0$ and $F_0$ is nonzero at a point, its observer energy there is positive and the residual is nonzero there; this does not estimate the distance to a different coupled solution.

Separately, let $\rho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega)$ and a $C^2$ future timelike field $U$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$ define charged dust on an open $\Omega\subseteq U$, with $\rho>0$, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and the formal matter-exchange equation of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. For any dimensionless $\eta>0$, replacing $(\rho,\sigma)$ by $(\eta\rho,\eta\sigma)$ multiplies $T_m$ and $j$ by $\eta$, leaves $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$ unchanged, and leaves the dust acceleration equation $\rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c$ unchanged when the prescribed $F$ and $U$ are held fixed. The sourced Maxwell equation must still match the changed current. If both $F$ and $j$ are scaled by $\eta$, Maxwell's equations remain linear but the electromagnetic stress scales by $\eta^2$, whereas the dust stress scales by $\eta$; no general coupled-solution family follows.

For a flat background with $\Lambda=0$ and $T_m=0$, a nonzero source-free Maxwell field cannot solve the exact Einstein equation with the unchanged Minkowski metric, because its observer energy density is positive somewhere.

Finally, in Minkowski space consider only the prescribed Coulomb profile on the finite annulus $\mathcal A_\ell:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3:\ell<|\mathbf x|<2\ell\}$, where $\ell>0$ is a length, $Q\ne0$ is a charge, $r:=|\mathbf x|$, $\mathbf e_r:=\mathbf x/r$, $\mathbf E(\mathbf x)=Q(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)^{-1}\mathbf e_r$, and $\mathbf B=0$.
